Volatility analysis of a coin

Source: R/fct_volatility.R
volatility_analysis.Rd

Is the coin's recent volatility normal? The analysis looks at the daily log returns, log(close(t) / close(t-1)), in two ways.

The last month (month_days days): its volatility, the standard deviation of the daily returns times sqrt(365), against the year before it and against every past period of the same length; an F test and the Fligner-Killeen test, which is robust to a few extreme days, of whether its variance is larger than the year before; its largest daily move, in standard deviations of the year before; and its return against every past period of the same length.

The last days (recent_days days): their return against every past period of as many days; the same, in standard deviations of the year before; a GARCH(1,1) model with Student-t errors (see garch_fit()), fitted to the garch_years years before them, which judges each day against the volatility the model expected for it given the days before; and each day's volume against the month_days days before it (see volume_ratio()), judged by how often the coin's volume was as far from usual.

The next days (forecast_days days): the same model, with its variance brought up to the last day, forecasts the volatility and the range of the price (see garch_forecast()), and gives the value at risk and the expected shortfall of the next day (see garch_risk()). A Kupiec test (see kupiec_test()) checks how often the model's value at risk was exceeded over the last year. The value at risk and expected shortfall of the last year's daily returns are given without the model too.

Usage

volatility_analysis(
  history,
  month_days = 30,
  recent_days = 2,
  garch_years = 4,
  forecast_days = 7,
  level = 0.95
)

Arguments

history

Price history of one coin from get_history(), sorted by date. The comparisons use the whole history, so pass all of it.

month_days

Days in the month.

recent_days

Days in the recent move.

garch_years

Years of history to fit the GARCH model to.

forecast_days

Days to forecast.

level

Probability of the forecast ranges, and of the value at risk: 0.95 is the 95% range and the worst 5% of days.

Value

NULL when the history is shorter than a year and a month, or the price did not move at all in the year before the month or the last days, otherwise a list with

  • coin, first_date and last_date;

  • month: a list of the month's measures, see the code;

  • recent: a list of the measures of the last days, with a days data frame of each day's return, GARCH measures, volume, volume_ratio and volume_one_in_days (NA without volume);

  • garch: the fitted model, or NULL when it could not be fitted or there are fewer than 500 days before the last days;

  • forecast: NULL without a model, otherwise a list with days, a data frame with a row per day ahead: its date, sigma (the daily standard deviation the model expects, in percent) and the closes low, low_50, median, high_50 and high of the ranges (see garch_forecast()); sigma and sigma_long_run, the daily standard deviation expected for the next day and in the long run; half_life, the days for the volatility to get half-way back to the long run; var and es, the value at risk and expected shortfall of the next day; and backtest, the days, exceedances and p_value of the Kupiec test;

  • history_risk: var and es of the daily returns of the last days (365) days, in percent;

  • series: a data frame with a row per day and the columns date, close, volume, return_pct, volume_ratio (see volume_ratio()), volatility_month (annualized, in percent), garch_sigma (the daily standard deviation the model expected, in percent), garch_z (the day's move in those standard deviations) and garch_var (the model's value at risk for the day, in percent);

  • settings: month_days, recent_days, garch_years, forecast_days and level.

Examples

btc <- get_history("Bitcoin (BTC)", as.Date("2013-04-29"))
analysis <- volatility_analysis(btc)
analysis$month$level
#> [1] "normal"
analysis$recent$days
#>         date return_pct     garch_z one_in_days      volume volume_ratio volume_one_in_days
#> 1 2026-11-05  -5.550836 -2.28819054   67.726837 48407763452     1.945375          15.237785
#> 2 2026-11-06  -0.257033 -0.09944261    2.276274 29286736588     1.146985           2.848965
analysis$forecast$days
#>         date    sigma      low   low_50   median  high_50     high
#> 1 2026-11-07 2.904263 71781.08 74783.24 75782.42 76794.94 80006.80
#> 2 2026-11-08 2.921028 70202.28 74319.64 75808.18 77362.61 81937.23
#> 3 2026-11-09 2.936918 69095.59 73951.74 75829.09 77802.22 83359.83
#> 4 2026-11-10 2.951984 68123.88 73678.62 75889.19 78202.65 84608.42
#> 5 2026-11-11 2.966272 67340.91 73403.37 75926.57 78561.40 85897.56
#> 6 2026-11-12 2.979826 66473.72 73186.09 75930.28 78862.33 87037.65
#> 7 2026-11-13 2.992688 65856.21 72949.92 75983.90 79140.42 88051.90
